posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
Ok, that iridescent posting got me thinking again. I mentioned this before, but I have a different spin on it. So I could use some advice on the matter.

If we make a hologram that replays within the wavelength of a "black light". Can we put a thin film of fluorescent material in front of it to see the hologram glow in the dark? My intuition tells me we will see something glowing but not the full depth of the image. In other words, will the full reconstructed wavefront fluorese?

What about if the hologram is not 3-d at all but rather a stereogram? Since each slit is 2-d, will this work?

Any thoughts?

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md:
Funny, how when you write something you think about it in a different way. I guess it would be pretty impossible to illuminate the fluoresent film with just the light off the hologram and not the raw illuminating light unless....

We polarize the light and the hologram changes the polarization that then goes though an opposite polarizer that then illuminates the fluoresent screen. (yes I just watched how LCD tv's work last night). Any light not altered by the hologram does not make it through the second cross polarizer.

posts.author: Danny Bee
posts.content_md:
> **JohnFP:** Funny, how when you write something you think about it in a different way. I guess it would be pretty impossible to illuminate the fluoresent film with just the light off the hologram and not the raw illuminating light unless....We polarize the light and the hologram changes the polarization that then goes though an opposite polarizer that then illuminates the fluoresent screen. (yes I just watched how LCD tv's work last night). Any light not altered by the hologram does not make it through the second cross polarizer.

If it was to work like the LCD panel the hologram would have to be transmission, but I think the problem is the type of light fluorescent gives off that makes it almost impossible. Even if you use it as a transient fluorescent screen you’re only getting an intersection of the light coming off the hologram. Remember a hologram is a mirror or lens redirecting the light to reconstruct the recorded wave front and is not the light. the only way I can see it might work is a focused image (image plain) hologram ,and it would be a dye phase hologram luminatied buy uv light, but again I think you get only a 2d glow.

posts.author: JohnFP
posts.content_md: Yea, that's what was bothering me, that 2-d fluoresent panel. Thanks for the confirmation. Like you say, if there was a cloud of fluoresent material in front of the hologram AND it was transmission AND it was image planed it may work.
